channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Após faltar a debate, Flávio Bolsonaro destaca ausência de Lula e diz querer debater com ele
item.description: After skipping the first 2026 presidential debate, Flávio Bolsonaro criticized Lula's absence and expressed interest in debating him directly.

item.title: Confira a agenda dos candidatos à Presidência nesta segunda-feira (24)
item.description: On Monday (24), presidential candidates continue their campaigns with various activities including town halls, interviews, public events, and sectoral meetings. Most candidates disclosed their agendas, except Lula and Rui Costa Pimenta. Pablo Marçal is barred from campaigning by the TSE.

item.title: TSE precisa acabar com dúvidas sobre uso de inteligência artificial antes do início do horário eleitoral, defendem ministros
item.description: TSE ministers advocate for the court to rule on AI usage in elections before the start of the free electoral time to avoid legal uncertainties. Current regulations prohibit deepfakes and AI-manipulated content when used to benefit or harm candidates. The case involves videos of Flávio Bolsonaro featuring AI-generated images of Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Saiba quais são as atribuições dos governadores e vice-governadores
item.description: In the 2026 elections, Brazilians will elect governors and vice-governors across all 27 federative units. The governor leads the state executive power, overseeing public policies in health, education, security, and infrastructure, and has the authority to sanction laws and manage state administration. The vice-governor, elected on the same ticket, replaces the governor during temporary absences or permanent vacancies.

item.title: “Quem votar em mim tem que votar no Flávio Bolsonaro”, diz Cleitinho
item.description: Minas Gerais gubernatorial candidate Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos) reinforced his support for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) for the presidency, stating that voters should support both. Despite the alignment, Flávio maintains rival candidate Flávio Roscoe as his pick for state governor. The senator claimed he lost Bolsonaro's rally in Minas but emphasized he will support him in other regions of Brazil.

item.title: Margem Equatorial: Petrobras prevê investimento bilionário em 15 poços
item.description: Petrobras plans to invest $2.5 billion in equatorial margin oil exploration, drilling 15 wells between 2026 and 2030. The company awaits environmental approval from Ibama to proceed. President Lula highlighted the recent oil discovery in the Amazon mouth as strategically important for global energy security.

item.title: No 1º turno, Lula tem 41% e Flávio Bolsonaro 37%, em empate técnico, aponta BTG/Nexus
item.description: A BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula with 41% and Flávio Bolsonaro with 37% in the first round, technically tied. The PT president leads the presidential race but Bolsonaro remains within the margin of error.

item.title: Vantagem numérica de Lula para Flávio diminui em 2° turno, ambos mantêm empate técnico, diz BTG/Nexus
item.description: Lula's numerical lead over Flávio Bolsonaro narrowed to 1 percentage point in a potential second round, keeping a technical tie, according to a BTG/Nexus survey released on August 24th.

item.title: Flávio tenta explicar ausência no debate da Band
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro explained his absence from the Band-sponsored presidential debate, claiming he wants to debate the main contenders. President Lula and Romeu Zema also skipped the first campaign debate.

item.title: Como está a disputa entre Lula e Flávio no maior colégio eleitoral do Brasil
item.description: A survey by Real Time Big Data shows that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) leads voter intentions in São Paulo, Brazil's largest electoral college, in both rounds — 38% in the first round and 49% in the second, compared to 33% and 44% for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). The poll surveyed 2,000 voters between August 19th and 22nd with a margin of error of two points and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: As oportunidades desperdiçadas por Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro ao fugirem do debate
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro skipped the debate organized by Bandeirantes, depriving the country of a key scrutinizing moment. Both evaded questions about scandals and contradictions, prioritizing their loyal base over the need to distinguish themselves.

item.title: Equipe de Flávio prevê programa de TV mais simples que o de Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign plans a simpler TV program than Lula's, due to less preparation time and recent departure of campaign strategists. The PT will have 5 minutes and 31 seconds of free advertising, while the PL will have 4 minutes and 20 seconds. The PL's strategy focuses on fewer scenes and lean production, contrasting with the PT's more elaborate approach.

item.title: TRE-SP rejeita recurso de Marçal e mantém inelegibilidade até 2032
item.description: TRE-SP rejected Pablo Marçal's appeal, maintaining his ineligibility until 2032 for creating a structure to pay influencers who produced campaign video edits, plus a R$420,000 fine. The ruling also denied the Public Ministry's request to expand the conviction due to insufficient evidence of actual prize payments. The TSE imposed precautionary measures barring Marçal from accessing electoral funds and participating in debates while reviewing his 2026 candidacy registration.

item.title: Agenda dos candidatos: Flávio Bolsonaro mira empresários em SP; Lula fica em Brasília
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) has a schedule in São Paulo with a Fiesp meeting and an entrepreneurship award, while Lula (PT) remains in Brasília without campaign activities on Monday. Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Romeu Zema (Novo) are also in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, respectively.

item.title: O cálculo de Zema ao fugir do debate da Band
item.description: Romeu Zema, candidate from the New Party for the Brazilian presidency, justified his absence from a Band TV debate by saying he prioritized studying for a TV Globo interview. His strategy aims to avoid mistakes in live broadcasts and focus on technical preparation for key debates.

item.title: Nova pesquisa mostra disputa eleitoral entre Tarcísio e Haddad em São Paulo
item.description: A recent poll released on Monday, 24, shows Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leading Fernando Haddad (PT) for São Paulo governor in the first round, with 52% of voting intentions against 35%. The incumbent governor's administration has a 63% approval rating and 31% disapproval, while Haddad leads in rejections at 38%.

item.title: Fachin recebe Janja para encontro no STF
item.description: STF president Edson Fachin meets with First Lady Janja da Silva to discuss actions against violence toward women, highlighting judicial strategies in the fight against femicide. The meeting will be used to present protective measures for women at risk.

item.title: Governo Lula discute reajuste diferente para beneficiários do INSS, diz jornal
item.description: Lula's economic team is considering differentiating the minimum wage adjustment between workers and INSS beneficiaries, keeping real gains for both groups but with different percentages. The measure aims to reduce pressure on mandatory expenditures and signal fiscal adjustment to the market.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: para 43%, governo Lula é ruim ou péssimo; 35% consideram ótimo ou bom e 22% regular
item.description: A BTG/Nexus survey shows that 43% of voters consider President Lula's government bad or very bad, while 35% rate it as good or excellent and 22% as fair. The survey was released on Monday, the 24th.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro seguem como mais rejeitados, com 49 % e 48%, respectivamente
item.description: A BTG/Nexus poll shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) top the list of most rejected presidential candidates, with 49% and 48% rejection rates respectively. The survey, released on March 24, indicates both figures are widely disliked among voters.

item.title: No 2º turno, Lula tem 46% e Flávio 45%, em empate técnico, aponta BTG/Nexus
item.description: A BTG/Nexus poll shows a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical runoff. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) secured 46% of voting intentions, while Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) obtained 45%.

item.title: Dos beneficiários do Bolsa Família, 61% votam em Lula e 27% em Flávio, diz pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: BTG/Nexus poll shows 61% of Bolsa Família beneficiaries intend to vote for Lula in the first round, while 27% support Flávio. Lula's vote intention dropped 4 percentage points from the previous survey.

item.title: Os efeitos para Ana Castela, após posar com Nikolas Ferreira em Barretos
item.description: Ana Castela posed with federal deputy candidate Nikolas Ferreira (PL) at the Barretos Rodeo Festival, sparking backlash on social media that led her to temporarily disable comments on Instagram. Singer Pabllo Vittar unfollowed the country artist following the controversial photo, while right-wing figures such as Flávio Bolsonaro and Tarcísio de Freitas were also present at the event. As of now, Ana Castela has not publicly commented on the controversy.

item.title: Veja Negócios anuncia as campeãs do ranking TOP 30 – As Melhores Empresas do Brasil
item.description: Veja Negócios held the awards ceremony for the winning companies of the TOP30 ranking, recognizing them for financial performance, governance, and sustainable growth. The event featured Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and highlighted Sabesp as the company of the year from the previous edition.

item.title: Datafolha, PEC do 6x1 e crise no STF: o raio-X da disputa presidencial
item.description: The 2026 political landscape shows Lula leading voter intentions over Flávio Bolsonaro, according to Datafolha, while other center and right-wing names remain stagnant. Meanwhile, Supreme Court investigations involving affiliates from both sides generate uneven impact, and Flávio faces isolation due to lack of support from traditional allies.

item.title: Sidônio Palmeira faz “dobradinha” entre Secom e campanha de Lula
item.description: The Minister of Communications, Sidônio Palmeira, plays an active role both in the government and in Lula's re-election campaign, joining the PT headquarters in Brasília. Despite being considered for departure from the government, his proximity to the president and influence on communication strategy ensure his stay.

item.title: Flávio encosta em Lula no 1º turno, indica Nexus
item.description: BTG/Nexus poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) catching up to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in the first round. Without Pablo Marçal (PRTB), the candidates are technically tied within the two-point margin of error. Lula leads with 41% of voting intentions.

item.title: Lula tem quase 30 pontos de vantagem sobre Flávio Bolsonaro na Paraíba, mostra pesquisa
item.description: A survey by Real Time Big Data shows President Lula (PT) leading with 55% of voting intentions in Paraíba against Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 26% in the first-round simulation, maintaining a 29-point advantage. Conducted between August 19 and 22 with 1,600 voters and a ±2 percentage point margin of error, the poll also indicates Lula ahead in a second-round scenario, with 59% versus 32%.

item.title: Governo Lula é desaprovado por 49% e aprovado por 48%, diz BTG/Nexus
item.description: A August 2026 BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula's government with 48% approval and 49% disapproval, with Lula leading first-round vote intentions (41%) against Flávio Bolsonaro (37%). Lula is also the most rejected candidate, with 49% saying they would never vote for him versus 48% for Flávio.

item.title: Quem é Augusto Cury, o escritor que disputa as eleições de 2026 e quer 'aumentar a régua do debate'
item.description: Augusto Cury, a 67-year-old writer and psychiatrist, is running for president in 2026 under the Avante party and participated in the first presidential debate on Band, where he criticized political polarization and advocated for civil discourse. He stood out for agreeing with Renan Santos on the need for change but disagreed with his aggressive tone when criticizing Lula's electorate. Cury positioned himself as an alternative to the center and far-right, seeking to elevate the quality of democratic debate.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: presidente Lula é aprovado por 48%; 49% o desaprovam
item.description: BTG/Nexus poll released on August 24 shows Lula with 48% approval and 49% disapproval, a technical tie. In head-to-head matchups, Lula leads the first round with 41%, against 37% for Flávio Bolsonaro; in second-round simulations, he is technically tied with both main opponents.

item.title: Quem dormiu antes de Kassab venceu o 'debate' presidencial
item.description: The Band presidential debate highlighted the absence of frontrunners like Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, leaving empty pulpits as the most striking scene. The edition was shortened due to low declared voting intentions on the network.

item.title: Após debate Band/Estadão, Caiado critica polarização fomentada por Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Following the Band/Estadão debate, Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized political polarization, blaming Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). He questioned how Congress can pass legislation amid such a divisive climate.

item.title: Kassab diz, após debate Band/Estadão, que Caiado critica tanto Lula quanto Flávio
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, running for vice president with the PSD, stated after the Band/Estado debate that federal deputy Ronaldo Caiado criticizes both Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Governor Flávio Dino, suggesting an unaligned stance toward either national leader.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro tem 5 pontos de vantagem na disputa com Lula em São Paulo, mostra pesquisa
item.description: A survey by Real Time Big Data shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 38% against Lula (PT) at 33% in the first round in São Paulo, with a five-point advantage. In the second round, the scenario evens out, with a technical tie within the margin of error, keeping Flávio numerically ahead.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: com 49%, Lula passa a ser mais rejeitado que Flávio, com 48%
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows that Lula leads first-round voting intentions but is the most rejected candidate at 49%, surpassing Flávio Bolsonaro (48%). In the second round, there is a technical tie between Lula and his main opponents.

item.title: O salto nos pedidos de reconhecimento de vínculo de emprego
item.description: Requests for employment bond recognition nearly tripled from 168,000 in 2020 to 471,000 in 2025, according to CNJ data. Delays in Supreme Court rulings on 'Uberization' and 'contracting' generate legal insecurity, worsening labor litigation. In an election year, Congress is unlikely to address the issue.

item.title: Lula supera Flávio em rejeição pela primeira vez desde abril, mostra nova pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: The latest BTG/Nexus poll shows that, for the first time since April, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has a higher rejection rate (49%) than Flávio Bolsonaro (48%), though the 1-point difference is within the margin of error. Despite this, Lula maintains a lead in voting potential, with 50% of respondents saying they would vote for him exclusively or among other options, compared to 47% for Flávio.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro empatam no 2º turno, mostra nova pesquisa Nexus/BTG
item.description: A new Nexus/BTG poll reveals a technical tie between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in a potential second round of the 2026 presidential election. The survey also shows Lula leading decisively against Romeu Zema (Novo), Renan Santos (Missão), and tying with Ronaldo Caiado (PSD). The poll was conducted between August 21 and 23 with 2,006 phone interviews and a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Onde Lula vence Flávio — e onde Flávio supera Lula — no segundo turno, segundo nova pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: A new BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula at 46% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 45% in a potential runoff, with the race remaining statistically tied. Voting preferences vary widely across gender, religion, region, and income, highlighting a deeply polarized electorate.

item.title: 50% veem possibilidade de interferência estrangeira nas eleições
item.description: Datafolha poll shows 50% of voters believe foreign interference in the 2026 elections is possible, with 32% viewing it as a problem and 18% not. The survey, filed with TSE, reveals notable differences between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro supporters, amid diplomatic tensions between Brazil, US and Argentina.

item.title: Flávio lidera disputa em SP com 38%, diz pesquisa Real Time Big Data
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leads surveyed voting intentions in São Paulo with 38%, followed by Lula (PT) at 33%. In a simulated runoff, Lula leads 49% to 44%. Survey of 2,000 voters conducted August 19–22 with a ±2 percentage point margin of error.

item.title: Nova pesquisa Nexus/BTG indica cenário apertado no 1º turno das eleições presidenciais
item.description: New Nexus/BTG poll shows a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of the 2026 presidential election, with 41% and 37% respectively in the first scenario. In a second scenario with Pablo Marçal, Lula leads with 40% against Flávio Bolsonaro's 34%, maintaining an advantage above the ±2 percentage point margin of error.

item.title: Real Time Big Data: Tarcísio tem 52% contra 35% de Haddad pelo governo
item.description: The Real Time Big Data survey shows Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leading with 52% of voting intentions, against 35% for Fernando Haddad (PT) in the race for governor of São Paulo. The 17-point lead indicates a first-round victory, with 63% approval for Tarcísio's administration.

item.title: Tarcísio tem 17 pontos de vantagem na disputa com Haddad, mostra pesquisa
item.description: A survey by Real Time Big Data shows that Sao Paulo governor Tarcisio de Freitas leads the race with a 17-point advantage over Fernando Haddad. The poll projects Tarcisio to win reelection in the first round with 52% of the votes.

item.title: Gusttavo Lima ignora vaias a Lula em Barretos, mas Globo exibe ‘climão’
item.description: During Gusttavo Lima's show in Barretos, part of the audience booed President Lula, but TV Globo did not broadcast the incident live. The singer, a Bolsonaro supporter, has endorsed the former president and once considered a 2026 presidential run but withdrew.

item.title: Saiba o que os candidatos ao Planalto farão nesta 2ª feira
item.description: Presidential candidates carry out official meetings and campaign events on August 24, 2026, highlighting interactions with economic leaders, ministers, and media interviews. Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Caiado, Zema, and Cury show varied schedules covering governance, productive sector engagement, and media presence. The programming reflects the advance of pre-campaigns with emphasis on economic and institutional matters.

item.title: Agenda de Lula: leia os compromissos do presidente nesta 2ª feira
item.description: President Lula has an official work schedule in Brasília on Monday, with meetings at Palácio do Alvorada and Palácio do Planalto. His commitments include meetings with advisors and ministers, as well as participation in the Contrata+Brasil event alongside Vice President Alckmin. The agenda reflects a focus on public management and ministerial relations.

item.title: Saiba quais pesquisas eleitorais podem sair nesta 2ª feira
item.description: Electoral polls registered with the TSE were authorized for release on Monday, August 24, 2026, covering electoral scenarios in 17 states and the Federal District. Disclosure depends on regulatory deadlines and contractor approval, with data accessible through the Poder360 Research Aggregator.

item.title: Governo Lula: leia a agenda de ministros do governo nesta 2ª feira
item.description: Ministers from President Lula's government carry out their work agenda in Brasília and via videoconference on Monday (24th). Key activities include meetings with the president at the Planalto, a session of the National Monetary Council, and the launch of a mental health service. The Chief of Staff, Finance, and Planning ministries lead the main movements of the day.
